criteria.statement: A designated authority states the North Star that KEEL is the portable, repository-native trust/control plane making high-autonomy Codex engineering governable, evidence-backed, recoverable, traceable, and delegable within the user's existing Codex/ChatGPT entitlement.
The authority states the fixed Codex and KEEL ownership boundary exactly.
The authority states exactly two legitimate KEEL operating surfaces and prohibits a second LLM runtime, model provider, generic conversation engine, or sandbox implementation.
ZERO_INCREMENTAL_COST is permanent and explicitly prohibits API keys, API billing, paid AI fallback, purchased-credit initiation, rate-limit circumvention, and KEEL-created AI billing paths.

The authority documents stable-versus-experimental Codex integration, safe degradation for unsupported stable capabilities, and no load-bearing experimental API dependency without separately authorized isolation.
The authority contains an ordered post-migration NS0-NS11 roadmap with NS0 as this reconciliation and NS1-NS11 derived from landed capability and ownership boundaries.

The authority resolves scheduler ownership by assigning deterministic WorkGraph reconciliation/resource scheduling to KEEL while Codex retains agent/runtime execution, explaining the prior contradiction.
Authoritative documents describe hooks only as guardrails/adapters and never as complete confinement.
Authoritative documents distinguish exact candidate verification from exact landed-state verification.
Every conflicting prior forward architecture/product-contract/roadmap document is marked superseded with a pointer while historical evidence is preserved.

Plans for the landed kernel migration, canonical ledger, RuntimeProfile/CapabilityGrant, desired-state scheduler, exact Git proof, candidate/landing attestations, public lifecycle UX, and separated KEELBench are reconciled to landed status using repository conventions.
No implementation behavior or non-documentation/non-plan-metadata file changes are made.
